posts.text: I haven‘t seen a movie in theaters since Top Gun: Maverick, so this will be the first one in years.

Williams hit .344 lifetime, including hitting .388 when he was pushing 40 year old.

Bonds hit .298 lifetime.  Pre-juice, he was a surefire HOF-er but not at Williams level as a hitter IMO.

Bonds as the Incredible Hulk in 2001 was the best hitter ever.  Just depends on how you want to slice it I guess.
That’s a shame because it was one of the best derby’s of all-time.

I’ve watched it but don’t necessarily subscribe to the obsession with modern analytics.  A guy that gets a hit 35% of the time is by definition a great hitter.  Oh, and I think Ted Williams had a pretty noteworthy OBP.

True, but he had his best years between ages 35 and 39, added 50 pounds of muscle, and grew his head to a size 8.  

Don't exactly need to stack inference upon inference to figure that one out.

Williams also didn’t have batting machines that mimicked the pitcher he was about to face.  

The guy would have lived in the cage if he had a Trajekt to work with.  

Something tells me he would have raked in any era.
